Champagne & Sparkling.say: Bubbles for a celebration. Champagne comes only from the Champagne region of France; Prosecco (Italy) is lighter and fruitier; Cava (Spain) is made the same way as Champagne.
Champagne & Sparkling.pair: Starters, shrimp cocktail, crab cake, fried dishes, birthdays and anniversaries.

Blush / Rosé.say: Pink wine made from red grapes with short skin contact. White Zinfandel is sweet; Provence rosé is dry, light and crisp.
Blush / Rosé.pair: Salads, salmon, chicken, Mediterranean and spicy dishes.

Moscato.say: Sweet, fruity and low in alcohol, with peach and honey notes. A good choice for guests who “don’t like dry wine”.
Moscato.pair: Desserts, fruit, spicy food, or on its own.

Riesling.say: Aromatic white with fresh acidity. German Kabinett is off-dry (slightly sweet); Alsace and Washington styles are crisper.
Riesling.pair: Spicy Asian and Indian dishes, pork, curry, jerk chicken.

Sauvignon Blanc.say: Crisp, zesty and refreshing, with citrus and green notes. New Zealand style is the most aromatic.
Sauvignon Blanc.pair: Salads, goat cheese tart, shrimp, white fish, vegetarian dishes.

Pinot Grigio.say: Light, dry and easy to drink, with apple, pear and citrus. Safe choice for most white-wine drinkers.
Pinot Grigio.pair: Light starters, white fish, seafood pasta, chicken.

Chardonnay.say: The world’s most popular white. Oaked styles (California) are rich and buttery with vanilla; unoaked styles are fresher and fruitier.
Chardonnay.pair: Lobster tail, salmon, creamy sauces, roast chicken, risotto.

Adventurous Whites.say: For guests who want something different: blends, Chenin Blanc and Albariño, aromatic with tropical and floral notes.
Adventurous Whites.pair: Seafood, shrimp, spicy or Asian dishes, Mediterranean food.

Pinot Noir.say: Light-to-medium red, soft tannins, red berries and cherry. The best red for guests who find red wine “too heavy”.
Pinot Noir.pair: Salmon, duck, chicken, mushroom dishes, pork.

Chianti.say: Italian red from Tuscany made mainly from Sangiovese: cherry, herbs and bright acidity.
Chianti.pair: Pasta with tomato sauce, lasagna, pizza, Italian night dishes.

Zinfandel.say: Bold, jammy red from California with ripe dark fruit and spice.
Zinfandel.pair: Barbecue, ribs, burgers, spicy meat dishes.

Malbec.say: Argentina’s signature red: dark, juicy and smooth, with plum and blackberry.
Malbec.pair: Steak, carne asada, grilled and braised meats.

Merlot.say: Medium-to-full red, smooth and plummy with soft tannins. Very approachable.
Merlot.pair: Roast beef, lamb, pork chop, pasta Bolognese.

Shiraz / Syrah.say: Full-bodied, peppery red with blackberry and spice. Australian Shiraz is rich and ripe.
Shiraz / Syrah.pair: Lamb, grilled steak, short rib, spicy dishes.

Cabernet Sauvignon.say: The king of red grapes: full-bodied, firm tannins, blackcurrant, cedar and vanilla.
Cabernet Sauvignon.pair: Prime rib, New York strip steak, filet mignon, lamb.

Master Red Blends.say: Wines blended from several grapes for balance and depth, from easy Côtes du Rhône to iconic Opus One.
Master Red Blends.pair: Steak, lamb, braised beef, rich meat dishes.

Adventurous Reds.say: Something different: Chilean Carménère, Spanish Tempranillo (Ribera del Duero) and Petite Sirah, all bold and dark-fruited.
Adventurous Reds.pair: Grilled and braised meats, lamb, Mexican and spicy food.
